target_customer: Pharmaceutical companies and drug developers who need crystal structure predictions for small molecule drugs
problem: Crystal structure affects drug stability and surprise polymorphs can force recalls. Lavo ran simulations and machine learning ranking to predict crystal structures faster than existing methods.
business_model: Simulation services and software sold to pharma
product_category: AI and quantum chemistry for drug formulation

founders.name: Scott Swarthout
founders.background_notes: YC launch post describes him as a former Google Cloud product manager; the YC company page lists software engineer at DoorDash and a former co-founder of Lavo. Roles conflict between pages.

founders.name: Zach Glick
founders.background_notes: PhD per the YC launch post.

founders.name: Derek Metcalf
founders.background_notes: PhD per the YC launch post; named principal investigator on the NSF SBIR award.

competitors.name: CCDC (Cambridge Crystallographic Data Centre)
competitors.what: Crystal structure database and informatics tools for pharma, launched CSD-Particle in 2022
competitors.funding_then: not stated, non profit data centre

competitors.name: XtalPi
competitors.what: AI drug discovery platform with crystal structure prediction
competitors.traction_then: worked with Pfizer on crystal structure prediction per a search summary

competitors.name: BioSimulytics
competitors.what: UCD spin out predicting polymorph landscapes from a 2D structure

technical_complexity.rationale: Crystal structure prediction needs accurate energy models from quantum chemistry plus machine learning to search a huge configuration space; the founders claimed 10x speedups after four months.

defensibility.rationale: Specialized computational chemistry expertise and validated models are hard to copy quickly, though academic methods and established vendors like CCDC and XtalPi were credible alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Lavo; the company kept publishing, with a July 2025 arXiv paper on automated crystal structure prediction listing Swarthout, Glick and Metcalf.

market_need_then: The YC launch post cites about 15,000 relevant drugs entering R&D each year and over $100M annual spending on crystal structure prediction, and uses the Ritonavir recall of the 2000s as the cautionary example.

branding.domain_note: Uses lavo.ai; founders listed as founders@lavo.ai on the YC page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and plain; launch post states simulations run on computers

brand_strength.rationale: A short, clean name appearing across many AI tool directories, but no press or community about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: The cause of Lavo's inactive status in the YC directory is not public. The company won an NSF SBIR Phase I grant of $274,990, listed a Phase II start of August 2024, and published a crystal structure prediction paper in July 2025, so it appears to have kept working after the batch. No shutdown or acquisition news was found, and directory listings still describe it as active, so the status may be stale. No failure factors are assigned.
notes: The lavo.ai fetch returned HTTP 503 so the live site was not checked. The $500K seed (La French Tech and Village listings) and the December 2023 BBQ Capital pre-seed (healthcare directory, amount undisclosed) each rest on a single aggregator; a Crunchbase page lists a pre-seed. The NSF grant is documented by HigherGov and Inknowvation, with the Phase II start 2024-08-31 per Inknowvation; one directory cites $1.49M total SBIR funding 2023 to 2027, unverified. Founder education and employers beyond the YC page are not sourced.
